clue.text: Approve Article 250,just before the end

parts.note: the indefinite article a
CCL is 250 in Roman numerals
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An instruction to approve a numbered legal article right before a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article 250' looks like a clause number in a statute; it is A plus the Roman numeral CCL, and 'just before' only places them ahead of AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim something is to praise it publicly, a strong form of approval.

clue.text: Deem a spinner to have dug out England's opener?

parts.note: a DJ spins records

indicators.note: out in the sense of wrong or disordered, so the letters of dug are rearranged
the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Thinking a spin bowler has managed to dismiss England's opening batsman in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner bowls and an opener bats first; here 'spinner' is a DJ, 'out' rearranges DUG to UDG, and England's opener is E.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjudge is to judge or consider formally, to deem something to be so.

clue.text: Great wall-light!?

parts.note: the Great Wall is in China, so a light from there is Chinese, and paper lights of that kind are hung up

explanation.definitionFit: Collapsible paper lamps of Chinese origin, hung as decorations, are lights from the land of the Great Wall.

clue.text: Correction-last word must go to chaps in data transmission

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, its last word

indicators.note: in says the chaps sit inside the abbreviation for data transmission

parts.note: DT is an abbreviation for data transmission
men, chaps

explanation.surface: Fixing a final word that has to be sent to some men over a data link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must go to' simply joins AMEN to the rest; MEN goes inside DT.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to correct or improve a text.

clue.text: Stage "Equus"

definitions.meaning: to stage a play is to put it on
Latin for horse, which is a rider's steed

explanation.surface: Putting on a production of Peter Shaffer's play Equus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equus' in quotes looks like the title of the play; it is used for its Latin sense, horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a show is to put it on, and a horse (Latin equus) is a rider's steed.

clue.text: Hide article in left ear

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here within the letter for left and the ear

parts.note: the definite article the

explanation.surface: Concealing a newspaper article in one's left ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin, which once tanned becomes leather.

clue.text: Wales soon suffers in time of reduced economic activity

indicators.note: suffers suggests damage, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: Wales will soon feel a downturn in its economy.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-peak period for tourism, when trade is quiet and prices fall, is the quiet part of the year.

clue.text: Boron found in adjutant's stomach

indicators.note: found in says boron sits inside the assistant

parts.note: an adjutant is an officer's assistant, an aide
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: A boron compound turns up in an army officer's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate it, to put up with it.

clue.text: He'll succeed if he isn't moved down the order

definitions.text: He'll succeed if he isn't moved down the order

parts.words: He'll succeed if he isn't moved down the order
parts.note: the next in line to a title, who inherits unless someone with a stronger claim, such as a later-born nearer relative, is born and displaces him

explanation.definitionFit: An heir whose right can be defeated by the birth of a closer claimant is next in line only by assumption.

clue.text: Following in Father's footsteps, by George?

definitions.text: Following in Father's footsteps, by George?

parts.words: Following in Father's footsteps, by George?
parts.note: 'by George' looks like an exclamation; it is the Prince of Wales, the future George IV, who ruled in place of his father George III

explanation.definitionFit: The period 1811 to 1820, when the Prince of Wales ruled in place of his ailing father, took its name from rule on behalf of a monarch.

clue.text: Enlisted in army—— clerical branch?

parts.note: signing up for the forces is to have joined up, and the clerical side of things is the writing; together they name a style of handwriting whose letters are linked

explanation.definitionFit: Cursive handwriting, with each letter linked to the next, goes by this name in British schools.

clue.text: Fear doctor initially lost head

indicators.note: initially lost says the word head drops its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A doctor who was afraid at first and then lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially lost' removes the H from HEAD, leaving EAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: English and Poles entering French class in morning break

indicators.note: entering says the poles and English letters go inside the French word

parts.note: eleves is French for pupils, a class of schoolchildren
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: An English contingent and Polish students join a French class for their mid-morning break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the compass poles N and S. NS and E go inside ELEVE-S, after the fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is a British snack and cup of tea taken around eleven o'clock, a break in the morning.

clue.text: Person approaching pieman without penny a hindrance? He was

definitions.text: Person approaching pieman without penny a hindrance? He was

parts.words: Person approaching pieman without penny a hindrance? He was
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Simple Simon met a pieman and wanted a pie, but had no penny to pay

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'Simple Simon met a pieman going to the fair'; the pieman asks to see his penny, and he has none.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish, gullible person is named after the nursery-rhyme boy who tried to buy a pie with no money.

clue.text: Poem discovered in Abu Simbel, Egypt

indicators.note: discovered in says the answer is found within the run of the place names

explanation.surface: A poem found carved at the ancient Egyptian temple of Abu Simbel.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, often a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Lift shown in architect's drawing?

definitions.meaning: raising something up, the act of lifting
a flat drawing of one face of a building

explanation.surface: A lift appears in the plans an architect has drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a raising up and an architect's view of a building's face from one side.

clue.text: Separate craft in which Father's conveyed

indicators.note: conveyed means carried, so the craft holds father inside it

parts.note: a craft is an art or skill
Pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A boat in which Dad is being transported somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a vessel; it is ART, a skill. PA sits inside it, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To be apart is to be separate, at a distance from each other.

clue.text: Australian came in looking shivery and washed-out

indicators.note: shivery means shaking, so the letters of came in are shaken up

explanation.surface: An Australian came indoors cold, trembling and pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone short of red blood cells looks pale and lacking colour, the sense of washed-out.

clue.text: Model of quadruped (tailless) associated with German author

parts.note: Thomas Mann, German novelist of The Magic Mountain

indicators.note: tailless says the word for horses drops its last letter

parts.note: equine, of a horse, the classic four-legged animal

explanation.surface: A model of a horse with its tail missing, linked to a German writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' takes the last E off EQUINE, leaving EQUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannequin is a dummy or a person used to model clothes.

clue.text: French negative about endless ticket problem something we've got to wear?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French negative goes round the rest

indicators.note: problem suggests trouble, so the letters are thrown into disorder
endless says the word ticket loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A Frenchman refuses because of a ticket problem, and wonders what to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last T from TICKET, 'problem' rearranges TICKE to ECKTI, and 'about' puts NE around it.

clue.text: Running Wolf, great western feature at the end of the day

definitions.text: western feature at the end of the day

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: Sounds like a Native American name, Running Wolf, a great figure in a cowboy western.

clue.text: Hoist is supporting article brought in by engineers

clue.text: Women give assistance to youngster

parts.note: help means assistance

clue.text: Jelly with a piquant flavour, almost

parts.note: a spice gives food a piquant flavour

explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Just one or two reds left?

parts.words: Just one or two reds left?
parts.note: reds are communists and the left is the political left; a follower of the two leaders of Soviet doctrine might be one of the few such believers left

clue.text: Small reservoir supplying domestic needs?

parts.note: a tank in the loft or above the toilet stores water for household use, a reservoir in miniature

clue.text: Long-accepted solution for conjunctivitis?

parts.note: solution suggests eye drops, but it is the answer to the puzzle: the familiar everyday name long used for an inflamed eye

explanation.definitionFit: The popular name for the eye inflammation conjunctivitis refers to the reddened colour of the white of the eye.
